iterations.title: World model in the control loop
iterations.question: Can a small JEPA-style world model improve grasp recovery?
iterations.evidence: 200 task attempts per controller across 5 conditions; missing-object stops were reported separately.
iterations.detail: Prediction error improved only slightly over the hold-current estimate. The planner did not improve overall task completion, so feedback stayed the default.

iterations.title: Keep the grasp offset consistent
iterations.question: Can one offset from open descent through closure reduce ranking errors?
iterations.evidence: 720 matched trials; 6 conditions; 40 trials per condition and controller.
iterations.measure: Feedback 150/200; original JEPA and coherent-offset variant 145/200 each.
iterations.detail: The coherent variant cut planning calls from 146 to 41. It had no paired wins and 5 losses against feedback. The change did not improve success or produce a material speed gain.

iterations.title: Predict finger contact
iterations.question: Can measured finger force give a better grasp signal than the held score?
iterations.evidence: 240 training, 80 validation, 80 test scenes; 40 new ranking scenes and 1,000 branches.
iterations.measure: Test macro AP 0.585 vs 0.223; Brier 0.068 vs 0.138. Ranking top choice: 25/40 vs 27/40 unchanged.
iterations.detail: Prediction improved overall, but red-cylinder recall stayed low. Candidate AP was 0.778 for the head and 0.738 for the old score. The contact head stayed out of the controller.

iterations.title: Target red-cylinder contact
iterations.question: Does targeted tipped-cylinder and slip data improve the weak object class?
iterations.evidence: 103 training, 24 validation, 40 test scenes; then 20 ranking scenes and 40 independent scenes.
iterations.measure: Red-cylinder AP 0.777 vs V3 0.732. Independent ranking: 20/40 vs 22/40 unchanged.
iterations.detail: Recall at a 0.5 threshold improved from 7.2% to 29.8%, but calibration stayed weak. The fresh independent ranking did not beat the unchanged grasp.
iterations.result: Better red-cylinder prediction; no ranking gain

iterations.title: Learn to rank grasp candidates
iterations.question: Can a tiny model combine contact forecasts and candidate geometry?
iterations.evidence: 40 training, 20 validation, and 40 test scenes; plus 40 fresh replication scenes. 1,000 branches in each test.
iterations.measure: First test: 29/40 vs 26/40 unchanged. Replication: 27/40 vs 25/40. Combined: 56/80 vs 51/80.
iterations.detail: The 241-parameter reranker had candidate AP 0.816 and 0.832 across the two audits; unchanged grasp AP was 0.777 and 0.801. Paired results: 12 wins, 7 losses, 61 ties (exact sign p=0.359). V6 later tested it as a recovery proposal; that test showed no task-success gain.
iterations.result: Small consistent contact-ranking lead; not a control result

iterations.title: Guarded world-model proposal with feedback recovery
iterations.question: Can a bounded model proposal help after feedback detects an empty grasp?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched red-cylinder task trials across five conditions, plus 8 missing-object checks; 8 task trials per condition.
iterations.measure: Feedback 26/40; hybrid 26/40. Paired outcomes: 0 wins, 0 losses, 40 ties (exact sign p=1.000).
iterations.detail: Feedback acted first. On recovery, the frozen JEPA and V5 ranker proposed a bounded grasp offset. Finger checks, camera replanning, and retries remained active. The ranker made 3 proposals during 17 retries; none changed task success. A feature audit found a contact-head channel mismatch in V5, so correct its inputs and retrain before another controller test.
iterations.result: No task-success gain; reranker features need correction

iterations.title: Correct the reranker inputs
iterations.kind: Corrected offline model and controller test
iterations.question: Does the corrected red-cylinder contact channel improve grasp ranking?
iterations.evidence: 40 fresh offline scenes with 1,000 branches; then 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Offline contact choice: 29/40 vs 27/40 unchanged. Controller: feedback and hybrid both 25/40.
iterations.detail: The corrected reranker used contact-head channel 3 for the red cylinder and removed the simulator-only tipped label. The controller had 0 wins, 0 losses, and 40 ties. Better contact ranking did not improve task success.
iterations.result: Better contact choice; no task gain

iterations.title: Fine-tune on fallen-cylinder scenes
iterations.question: Can extra fallen-object demonstrations improve the VLA policy?
iterations.evidence: 240 training scenes, 60 validation scenes, and 40 matched task trials.
iterations.measure: Tipped waypoint error fell from 7.15 mm to 6.08 mm. Task success fell from 21/40 to 19/40.
iterations.detail: The adapted policy improved its tipped-scene waypoint metric but lost two task successes overall. It had 1 win and 3 losses against the base policy. Keep the base policy as the default.
iterations.result: Better waypoint metric; worse task result

iterations.title: Retry with the last valid visual plan
iterations.question: Can a saved visual target help when the camera briefly loses the object?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks on fresh seeds.
iterations.measure: Feedback 21/40; hybrid 21/40. The fallback ran 30 times.
iterations.detail: The first low-confidence view still stopped the controller. A saved target was used only after a prior valid view and during bounded recovery. It did not add a successful task.

iterations.title: Test visual routing to the adapted policy
iterations.question: Can a small visual gate select the adapted policy only for a fallen object?
iterations.evidence: Three gates tested on 40 fresh tipped and 40 fresh upright scenes each.
iterations.measure: Best tipped-object recall was 5%, with a 2.5% false-positive rate. No controller test was run.
iterations.detail: A linear gate, a small MLP, and a crop classifier all missed most fallen cylinders. The gate did not meet the fixed validation limit, so the routed model stayed out of the controller.

iterations.title: Relax the proposal gate
iterations.question: Will more frequent recovery proposals turn contact ranking into task gains?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Feedback and hybrid both 24/40; 0 wins and 0 losses.
iterations.detail: The permissive gate accepted all four non-default proposals. None changed the final task result. The missing-object safe-stop rate stayed 7/8 for both.

iterations.title: Use the reranker on the first grasp
iterations.question: Can a grasp proposal help before the first failed attempt?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Feedback and hybrid both 23/40; 2 wins, 2 losses, and 36 ties.
iterations.detail: The ranker changed 41 grasp commands. Two feedback failures became successes, but two successful feedback trials became failures. The net task result was unchanged.

iterations.title: Rank grasps by complete task success
iterations.question: Does a ranker trained on full pick, lift, and place outcomes improve the controller?
iterations.evidence: Offline: 12/40 vs 4/40 successful grasp choices. Primary controller test: 30/40 vs 26/40. Independent replication: 27/40 vs 25/40.
iterations.measure: Across 80 matched trials: V13 57/80; feedback 51/80. Paired results: 11 wins, 5 losses, and 64 ties (exact p=0.210).
iterations.detail: Both fresh seed ranges favored V13. The combined gain is 6 tasks, but the paired test is small and does not establish a reliable effect. Missing-object safe stops were 15/16 for both controllers. Keep testing in simulation before any real-arm use.

iterations.title: Plan from the parked camera view
iterations.question: Can the controller skip its initial probe-and-return without reducing task success?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched hybrid task trials on the same fresh seeds; plus 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Original and direct-approach hybrid both completed 21/40 tasks. Paired outcomes: 0 wins, 0 losses, 40 ties. Inference calls fell from 122 to 89.
iterations.detail: V14 follows the first camera plan from the parked pose. It skips the first approach, retreat, and second pregrasp inference. Finger checks, retries, and the post-lift camera replan remain active. Both controllers stopped safely in 8/8 missing-object checks. Mean control time did not improve: 2.06 s for the original and 2.19 s for V14.

iterations.title: Run trials on the articulated B601-RS arm
iterations.question: Can a joint-limited pick-and-place run on the B601-RS model without the Panda surrogate?
iterations.evidence: 12 seeded red-cube trials with small randomized starts; 3 selected videos. The teacher reads simulator state.
iterations.measure: 12/12 placements; all six arm joints stayed within their URDF limits. Speed and gripper conversion still need calibration.
iterations.detail: The trials load Seeed’s B601-RS URDF in PyBullet, use its six arm joints and two prismatic fingers, and move with quintic joint-space profiles. The reference peaks at up to 2.25 rad/s, above Seeed’s 1.50 rad/s web target limit; the finger motor-to-width conversion is not reproduced. This validates the articulated simulator path, not a learned VLA or a controller-faithful speed and gripper stack.
